_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Australia covering Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples (65,000+ years continuous habitation, oldest living cultures on Earth), Dutch exploration (1606 Janszoon, 'New Holland'), British colonisation (1770 Cook, 1788 First Fleet/Botany Bay, penal colony), frontier wars and dispossession, six colonies federated 1901 (Commonwealth of Australia), White Australia Policy (1901-1973, Immigration Restriction Act), Gallipoli 1915 (ANZAC legend, national myth), WWII (Darwin bombing, Kokoda, Pacific War alliance with US), post-war immigration boom (Mediterranean/European, multiculturalism), Whitlam dismissal 1975 (constitutional crisis), reconciliation movement, Stolen Generations apology 2008 (Rudd), 2023 Voice referendum failed, AUKUS alliance.

religion.note: Rapid secularisation (No religion fastest-growing, 2021 census passed Christianity decline); historically Anglican/Catholic (Irish convict legacy, sectarian divide faded); multicultural immigration brought Islam/Hinduism/Buddhism/Sikhism; Aboriginal spirituality (Dreaming/Dreamtime, sacred sites Uluru, not census-captured); Catholic largest single denomination (~20%); Pentecostal (Hillsong Church global HQ); school chaplains controversial; marriage equality 2017 postal survey (61.6% yes)

ethnic_groups.name: European ancestry
ethnic_groups.notes: English/Irish/Scottish/Welsh dominant (~36% English, ~11% Irish, ~9% Scottish); convict origins (1788-1868, 162k transported); free settlers; Gold Rush 1850s; post-WWII immigration (British '£10 Poms'); cultural cringe vs nationalism; 'Aussie' identity (egalitarian, larrikin, mateship, fair go); suburban; sport (cricket, AFL, rugby, swimming); six-state federalism; British Crown (constitutional monarchy, King Charles III)

ethnic_groups.name: Asian ancestry
ethnic_groups.notes: Chinese (~5.5%, largest non-European group, Gold Rush 1850s, White Australia exclusion, post-1973 return, 2020s tensions with PRC, skilled migration), Indian (~3.1%, fastest growing, IT/healthcare, Sikh community), Vietnamese (~1.3%, refugees 1975-80s boat people), Filipino (~1.3%), Korean, Japanese; Asian immigration transformed Australia post-1970s; integration largely successful; 'Yellow Peril' panic to Asian Century pivot

ethnic_groups.name: Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander
ethnic_groups.notes: ~983k (2021 census, growing due to identification); 65,000+ years continuous habitation (oldest living cultures on Earth); 250+ language groups at colonisation (most now endangered/extinct); Stolen Generations (1910-1970, forcible removal of children, assimilation policy, Rudd apology 2008 'Sorry'); life expectancy gap 8 years; incarceration 12x rate; deaths in custody; Uluru Statement from the Heart 2017; Voice referendum 2023 (60% No, devastating); Native Title (Mabo 1992, overturned terra nullius); land rights; Dreaming/Dreamtime (spiritual framework, songlines); dot painting; didgeridoo; ongoing systemic disadvantage

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Middle Eastern/North African (~3%, Lebanese/Iraqi/Afghan, Cronulla riots 2005), African (~2%, Sudanese/South Sudanese/Somali, recent, integration challenges, 'African gangs' controversy Melbourne), New Zealander (~2.5%, free movement, 'across the ditch'), Pacific Islander (~1.5%, Samoan/Tongan/Fijian); multicultural policy since 1970s (Whitlam/Fraser); immigration central to economy (~190k/year permanent, backpackers, students, temporary visa workers); refugee policy harsh (offshore detention Nauru/Manus Island 2013-23, 'Stop the Boats', Operation Sovereign Borders, international condemnation)

country_profile.time_zone: AEST (UTC+10), ACST (UTC+9:30), AWST (UTC+8); daylight saving varies by state

independence.from: Federation of six British colonies into Commonwealth of Australia; Statute of Westminster adopted 1942 (backdated to 1939); Australia Act 1986 (full legal independence from UK Parliament)

country_profile.notes_unique: Oldest continuous cultures on Earth (Aboriginal Australians 65,000+ years, Dreaming/songlines, dot painting, boomerang, didgeridoo); largest island/smallest continent (7.7M km², 6th largest country); convict origins (1788 First Fleet, 162k transported, penal colony, bushranger mythology Ned Kelly); White Australia Policy (1901-1973, explicitly racist immigration restriction, dictation test, shaped homogeneous society, dismantled under Whitlam); ANZAC legend (Gallipoli 1915, WWI defining national myth, April 25 ANZAC Day most sacred national day, 'lest we forget', Kokoda WWII); Stolen Generations (Aboriginal children forcibly removed 1910-70, assimilation, trauma, Rudd 'Sorry' speech Feb 2008); Great Barrier Reef (UNESCO, largest coral reef system, 2,300km, climate change bleaching crisis); Uluru/Ayers Rock (Anangu sacred site, climbing banned 2019); fauna (kangaroo, koala, platypus, 80%+ endemic species, deadly animals stereotype); bushfires (Black Summer 2019-20, 46M acres burned, 3B animals, climate change); sport (cricket Ashes, AFL uniquely Australian, rugby, swimming, Melbourne Cup 'race that stops a nation'); mining boom (iron ore, coal, LNG, China dependence); AUKUS (2021, Australia/UK/US security pact, nuclear submarines, China containment); offshore detention (asylum seekers, Nauru/Manus Island, 'Pacific Solution', international condemnation, bipartisan policy); multiculturalism (post-1970s, remarkably successful integration, 30% foreign-born, 50%+ first/second generation immigrant); housing crisis (Sydney/Melbourne unaffordable, negative gearing); coffee culture; vegemite; 'no worries mate'

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Anthony Albanese
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: Labor; first PM from public housing; 'Albo'; won 2022 election ending 9 years of Liberal-National coalition; Voice to Parliament referendum 2023 (failed 60% No, defining defeat); AUKUS continuation; housing crisis; cost-of-living; stage 3 tax cuts revised; republic debate shelved; pragmatic left

head_of_state.name: King Charles III
head_of_state.title: King of Australia
head_of_state.notes: Constitutional monarch; represented by Governor-General Sam Mostyn (since July 2024, first female in 3 decades); 1999 republic referendum failed (54.87% No, split between minimalist/direct-election models); monarchy stable but republican sentiment exists

former_leaders.name: Scott Morrison
former_leaders.notes: Liberal; 'ScoMo'; Hawaii during bushfires (2019-20, PR disaster); COVID response (closed borders, Fortress Australia); AUKUS deal; submarine contract broke France deal; secret ministries scandal (appointed himself to 5 portfolios secretly, unprecedented, found unlawful); lost 2022 (teal independents, climate shift)

former_leaders.name: Malcolm Turnbull
former_leaders.notes: Liberal; ousted Abbott (spill); same-sex marriage postal survey 2017 (61.6% yes); moderate; NBN; ousted by own party (Dutton challenge, Morrison compromise)

former_leaders.name: Tony Abbott
former_leaders.notes: Liberal; 'Stop the Boats' (Operation Sovereign Borders); climate sceptic (repealed carbon tax); knighted Prince Philip (ridiculed); ousted by Turnbull

former_leaders.name: Kevin Rudd
former_leaders.notes: Labor; Sorry speech 2008 (Stolen Generations, historic); ratified Kyoto Protocol; GFC stimulus ('cash splash', Australia avoided recession); ousted by Gillard 2010; returned briefly 2013; lost election; later Ambassador to US

former_leaders.name: Julia Gillard
former_leaders.notes: Labor; first female PM; minority government (Greens/independents); carbon tax (then ETS); misogyny speech (2012, viral, against Abbott); NDIS architect; undermined by Rudd destabilisation; 'Ju-liar' attacks; polarising but substantive

former_leaders.name: John Howard
former_leaders.notes: Liberal; 2nd longest-serving (11 years); gun control (Port Arthur 1996, 35 dead, banned semi-automatics, buyback, no mass shootings since); GST introduction; Tampa affair 2001 (asylum seekers, 'Pacific Solution'); Iraq War 2003 (Bush/Blair ally); WorkChoices (lost him 2007 election, lost own seat); 'Honest John' to supporters, divisive to critics

former_leaders.name: Paul Keating
former_leaders.notes: Labor; Redfern Speech 1992 ('We did this', Aboriginal acknowledgement); Mabo (Native Title Act 1993); republic push; 'banana republic' warning; Asia engagement; compulsory superannuation; 'the recession we had to have'; sharp wit; most quotable PM

former_leaders.name: Bob Hawke
former_leaders.notes: Labor; most popular PM; Accord (wages, unions); floated dollar; deregulated economy; Medicare; Tiananmen Square (offered asylum to Chinese students); 'any boss who sacks a worker for not turning up [day after America's Cup] is a bum'; larrikin legend; died 2019

former_leaders.name: Gough Whitlam
former_leaders.notes: Labor; transformative (ended White Australia Policy, free uni, Medibank, recognized China, no-fault divorce, Indigenous land rights); 1975 Dismissal (Governor-General Kerr sacked him, constitutional crisis, 'Well may we say God save the Queen', most polarising event in Australian political history); lost 1975 election; died 2014; Labor hero
